question: Which LLTO coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, how does it compare with the pristine NCM, and why did the 2 mol.% coating lower the rate capability?
expect: LLTO-2, 86.2% (LLTO-0.5 85.5%, LLTO-1 57.2%) vs 56.6% pristine (p10.L22-25); the thicker 2 mol.% layer suppressed electron transfer (p10.L17-20)
rendered:
According to the text, LLTO coated NCM retained about 85.5% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C. This is compared to the pristine NCM, which retained 56.6% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles. The LLTO coating helped prevent direct contact between the cathode material and the electrolyte, thus suppressing unwanted side reactions. 

The 2 mol.% coating lowered the rate capability because it increased the thickness of the coating layer, which resulted in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.
